item.title: Four Killed, 16 Injured In Lagos Road Accident
item.description: Four people have been reported killed, while 16 others were injured in an accident on Alaro City Bridge after a truck carrying a container overturned on a passenger bus at Berger Bridge, inward Eleko, along the Ibeju-Lekki Expressway in Lagos. The accident occurred in the early hours of Wednesday, according to the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA). While providing further details, the Agency noted that the articulated truck conveying a 20-foot container with an unknown registration number and a Toyota Hiace with registration number GME-589 ZU collided due to overspeeding, with the truck ascending the bridge at high speed, losing control, and overturning onto the bus. According to the Permanent Secretary of LASEMA, Dr. Olufemi Damilola Oke-Osanyintolu, they received a distress call regarding the fatal accident, and the ‘Beta Whales Team’ from Epe Base was deployed to the scene immediately. LASEMA also noted that the impact of the collision was severe. “The impact was severe and tragically resulted in the loss of four (4)adult males who were confirmed dead at the scene, while sixteen (16)other adult males sustained varying degrees of injuries. The Agency said the recovery operation is ongoing, and traffic management measures have been deployed to ensure safety. LASEMA towing truck involved in the accident Reacting to the development, the Lagos State Government commiserated with the families of the deceased and wished the injured victims a speedy recovery. Another truck accident was also reported around Vetland School, inward Agege Pen Cinema along Old Abeokuta Road at around 4:09 am, with the Tiger Team from C3 Base responding to the accident. The agency said the team observed a truck with registration number KTU-940XT which had rammed into a solar-powered streetlight pole before mounting the road median and obstructing vehicular movement as a result of reckless driving. According to the agency, they immediately implemented traffic diversion to prevent secondary incidents and to ease movement. “With the arrival of the Agency’s heavy-duty recovery equipment, Elephant, the affected truck was successfully recovered and conveyed to Abattoir Police Station for further investigation and safekeeping. The roadway has since been cleared and reopened for normal vehicular movement”. LASEMA also reported another accident at Igando along LASU-Igando road at Lanre Bus stop involving a DAF Truck with registration number SMK 795 XY which collided with a Toyota Corolla with registration number AKD 169 EA. They said, “Information gathered at the scene indicated that while a broken-down truck on the other side of the road had caused traffic build-up, the DAF Truck driving against traffic collided with the Corolla, blocking half of the road inward to Igando”. item.title: Nigeria would be rich if leaders left public funds in banks – Obi
item.description: Former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi has said Nigeria would be significantly wealthier if leaders left public funds in banks to generate interest instead of mismanaging the country’s resources. Obi, who is the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) for the 2027 general elections, made the statement during an interview with a radio station in Nasarawa State on Wednesday, where he spoke about his administration’s approach to public spending, accountability and his record in basic education. The former Labour Party presidential candidate argued that the country could have accumulated substantial wealth if public office holders consistently protected government funds and allowed them to earn interest in financial institutions. “I wish everybody in this country left money in the bank; they have interest. Nigeria would have been so rich that we don’t know what to do with money,” he said. Obi disclosed that the funds under his administration were kept in three different banks, presenting the decision as an example of prudent management of public resources. He also lamented what he described as a culture of dishonesty and the tendency to discredit people who act with integrity in Nigeria. “Nigeria is a criminalised place. The criminals will always come together to show what the honest person did,” he said. The former governor further criticised what he described as a reversal of moral values, arguing that people who act honestly are often treated as though they have committed wrongdoing. “In Nigeria, to be honest is to be a criminal. To be criminal is to be honest,” Obi said. He added that Nigeria would have accumulated far greater wealth if its leaders had consistently left public funds in banks rather than diverting them. “We would have been worth so much that we don’t know what to do with money,” he said. Obi also addressed questions surrounding his administration’s public engagements, explaining that he believed the results of government projects should speak for themselves because they were financed with public funds. “We did what we were doing with public money, so the public already see us working, so why are we going to do the ceremony or showing it on TV? Maybe I was wrong, but that was what happened,” he said. The former governor also defended his record in basic education, insisting that Anambra performed exceptionally well in the sector during his tenure. “I was the best in education, basic education as a governor. You can go and check the records,” he said. He cited a visit by Professor Paul Collier of the University of Oxford, whom he said visited several states to assess developments in education and witnessed significant improvements. Obi maintained that education was a key measure of development and argued that his administration’s performance in the sector demonstrated the impact of responsible leadership. item.title: The Signal: The Parties Are Choosing Sides. Will the Voters Follow?
item.description: Tinubu’s political alliances are expanding, Obi and Kwankwaso are sharpening their challenge, and INEC is under pressure to demonstrate transparency. But as the presidential campaign gathers momentum, Nigeria’s politicians may be discovering that winning endorsements is easier than winning public confidence. There is an interesting contradiction emerging in Nigerian politics. At a time when political parties are supposed to be competing against one another, their leading figures are increasingly finding reasons to work together. In Rivers State, Nyesom Wike is assembling a coalition that crosses party boundaries but supports President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates. In Osun, Governor Ademola Adeleke supports Tinubu’s re-election while insisting that his political organisation will compete against the APC in legislative elections. Meanwhile, Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso have established a joint presidential campaign structure, even as other opposition leaders continue discussing the possibility of a broader alliance. And the Independent National Electoral Commission, caught in the middle of growing political suspicion, has taken a step towards addressing concerns about the voters’ register. Welcome to Nigeria’s 2027 election. A contest in which party labels are becoming increasingly flexible, political loyalties are being renegotiated, and the electorate is being asked to distinguish between genuine conviction and political convenience. But beneath the manoeuvring lies a question that could determine the outcome. The politicians are choosing sides. Will the voters follow them? Wike’s coalition: when political boundaries become optional Nyesom Wike has never been a politician easily constrained by conventional party loyalties. His support for Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, despite his association with the PDP, demonstrated his willingness to pursue political objectives across party lines. Now, with another presidential election approaching, he is taking that approach further. At a political gathering in Eleme, Rivers State, Wike made it clear that his Rainbow Coalition is not simply an arrangement to support Tinubu’s re-election. It also intends to support APC candidates contesting governorship and legislative elections. That is a significant development. It suggests that Wike is attempting to create a political structure capable of influencing elections at several levels, regardless of the formal party affiliations of those participating. There is a certain political logic to the arrangement. For Tinubu, Wike provides an influential ally in a strategically important state. For Wike, cooperation with the President offers a means of preserving political relevance and strengthening his position in Rivers. But what does the arrangement offer ordinary voters? item.title: Iran warns any Israeli-led attack would be ‘devastating’ for global markets
item.description: Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned on Wednesday that any Israeli-instigated attack in the Gulf region would have a “devastating impact” on global markets. “Devastating impact on int’l markets of any Israel-instigated military misadventure in Persian Gulf region remains major concern for both gas suppliers and consumers,” Araghchi said in a post on X. The United States and Israel have in recent days raised the prospect of renewed attacks on Iran in the Middle East war which began in February with strikes on the Islamic republic. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is seeking to form a new government after close elections, said on Wednesday he could work with US President Donald Trump to eliminate the “existential threat” posed by Iran. item.title: Military arrests two over attack on vigilantes, burning of Jos office
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa Troops of Operation Enduring Peace, OPEP, have arrested two suspects over an alleged attack on members of a vigilante group and the subsequent burning of their office in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The suspects were arrested at about 1:40 a.m. on October 27, 2026, in the NEPA area of Jos North. Media Information Officer of OPEP, Capt. Chinonso Polycarp Oteh, who confirmed the arrests, said the suspects were apprehended by troops of Sector 1, OPEP. Oteh said, “The arrest followed allegations linking the suspects to the attack on vigilante personnel and the subsequent setting ablaze of their office.” He said, “The suspects are currently in custody for further investigation and necessary action.” Oteh said, “The arrests form part of ongoing efforts by OPEP to tackle criminal activities and maintain peace across Plateau State.” He added, “Security personnel will continue to intensify operations aimed at identifying and apprehending individuals involved in acts capable of undermining peace and security in the state.” ” We call on members of the public to cooperate with the military and other security agencies by providing timely and credible information that could assist in preventing criminal activities and apprehending suspects.” Oteh said, “The continued cooperation and support of members of the public remain crucial to our efforts to maintain peace and security across the state.” He added, “Security personnel will continue to intensify operations aimed at identifying and apprehending individuals involved in acts capable of undermining peace and security in the state.” The post Military arrests two over attack on vigilantes, burning of Jos office appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Real Madrid apologise to China over Mbappe comments
item.description: Real Madrid apologised to China on Wednesday for Kylian Mbappe’s comments poking fun at Mao Zedong, after the star striker’s remarks sparked a social media storm and saw Spanish football yanked off state TV. Mocking former leader Mao — blamed by historians for millions of deaths — is taboo in China, and Mbappe’s remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure to anger Beijing. In a clip of a video interview with French show “The Bridge” — since taken down — Mbappe talked about being amused by an internet meme of his face photoshopped onto “some guy, think he’s a Chinese dictator”, an apparent reference to Mao. Real Madrid “wishes to express its apologies to the Chinese people for any offence caused by the recent remarks of our player Kylian Mbappe”, the club said in a statement. “The club joins in the public apology issued by Kylian Mbappe, in which the player himself expressed his regret for his words and reiterated his respect for the Chinese people,” the 15-time European champions said. The statement came a day after Mbappe issued his own apology, in French, Chinese and English, saying: “My comment was ill-judged and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world.” Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing on Wednesday: “We take seriously the apology the individual concerned has made.” La Liga, which saw the broadcast of its matches suspended in China, said Tuesday it “deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans”. Earlier, the state-run Global Times said in an editorial that it was “not difficult to see that the club’s longstanding tolerance of such behavior has contributed to Mbappe’s latest offensive remarks”. Chinese beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year’s World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe, said Tuesday it had scrapped its partnership with the player, as did dairy firms Mengniu and Milkground. CMG, which oversees public broadcaster CCTV, said it had decided to suspend broadcasts of La Liga, the world’s second-richest football league after England’s Premier League. Mbappe, 27, continued to face a torrent of criticism from Chinese web users on Wednesday, some of it racist. “His remarks were hurtful toward China and the Chinese people, so they cannot be translated,” wrote one user on social media platform Weibo. Mbappe’s original joke about Mao was not reposted — or had been scrubbed — from China’s tightly controlled social media. Chinese social media app Xiaohongshu had meanwhile frozen Mbappe’s account, where he has over a million followers. The same was done on the Weibo app, with a notice stating that “the user has been banned from following due to violating laws or the Weibo Community Convention”. item.title: Court dismisses Emeka Ike’s N10bn damages suit against Wike’s aide, INEC
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Wednesday dismissed N10 billion rights suit filed by the Nollywood actor Emeka Ike against Lere Olayinka, Senior Special Assistant to FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Justice Salim Ibrahim, in a judgment, upheld the preliminary objections of the respondents on the grounds that the suit was incompetent and improperly constituted. Justice Ibrahim also dismissed the main suit on the ground of lack of proof. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Ike, who aspired to vie for the House of Representatives’ seat for AMAC/Bwari Federal Constituency, Abuja, for the 2027 general elections on the platform of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC), lost the bid in a primary poll. The FCT minister’s aide, through a post on X in May, was alleged to have mocked Ike by leaking his confidential voter registration details on social media. The post was said to have shown details of Ike’s voter registration transfer from Imo to the nation’s capital. Meanwhile, Ike, in the suit filed by L. T. Adeh, sued Olayinka and INEC as 1st and 2nd respondents in the suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1272/2026. He asked the court to declare that Olayinka’s decision to publish his database on X without his approval “amounts to gross breach and violation of the applicant’s fundamental right to privacy and the protection of personal data”. Ike argued that Section 37 of the 1999 Constitution, Article 12 of the universal declaration of human rights, and Sections 24 & 39 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 guaranteed his right to privacy and protection of personal data. The actor asked the court to declare that INEC owes him and other voters a “statutory duty of care” to protect their private data against unauthorised access. The applicant, therefore, prayed the court to award him N10 billion against Olayinka and INEC as aggravated and general damages, to be paid jointly and severally for violating his fundamental right to privacy. He sought a declaration that the press release by INEC dated June 2, in reaction to the viral publication and circulation of his personal voter information and private data on social media by Olayinka, amounts to a tacit admission of guilt and liability to him. Ike, equally, sought an order directing Olayinka to immediately retract and pull down the offensive post and publication on his social media X handle, @OlayinkaLere, containing screenshots of his personal voter information and private data. He sought an order directing him to immediately tender an unravelling apology in writing for breach and violation of his fundamental right. But responding in a separate counter-affidavit, INEC and Olayinka prayed the court to dismiss the suit in its entirety. INEC, in its response, said the issue complained about in the suit filed by Ike was neither classified, sensitive nor confidential information. item.title: Thierry Henry explains Yamal joke after fans accuse him of disrespect
item.description: Former Arsenal and France striker Thierry Henry has explained his controversial remarks about Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal during the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony, insisting that he had no intention of disrespecting the young footballer. Henry, who co-hosted the awards ceremony alongside Kate Scott on Monday, faced criticism after jokingly questioning whether Yamal really wanted the Kopa Trophy, an award presented to the best young player in world football. Yamal won the trophy for the third consecutive time, but Henry’s comments sparked reactions from fans who interpreted them as a suggestion that the teenager was overly concerned about winning individual honours. Responding to the backlash in a video shared on Instagram, Henry said his remarks had been misunderstood, stressing that he was a huge admirer of the Barcelona star. “For Lamine Yamal, I wasn’t checking his ego at all. I just thought that, as the third time that he’s winning that trophy, I just asked him if that’s the one that he really wanted,” he said. The former Barcelona forward explained that he had expected Yamal to compete for the main Ballon d’Or award, which was eventually won by England captain Harry Kane. “I am a big fan of Lamine Yamal. I wasn’t checking his ego whatsoever. That you didn’t like the joke, I can understand, but please don’t do that. He’s one of the players that I will pay to watch. I love him,” Henry added. He described Yamal as an exceptional talent whose performances he enjoys watching, expressing regret that the youngster did not claim the night’s biggest prize. “Unfortunately, he didn’t win it, because he’s a hell of a player that I enjoy to watch,” he said. Henry also addressed a separate controversy involving his co-host, Scott, after viewers criticised him for making a joke about her pronunciation of the name Socrates, the late Brazilian football legend. The former France international denied disrespecting Scott, maintaining that the exchange was planned and that she was aware of the joke before it was delivered. “Kate was with me on that joke,” Henry said. “And you can ask Kate, by the way. She did it on purpose, to say Socrates. And I had to say Socrates [with a different pronunciation].” He urged critics to stop portraying the exchange as an attempt to embarrass his colleague. “Again, that you didn’t like the joke, I understand. But please stop saying that I disrespect Kate. I will never do that,” he added. The 49-year-old further clarified his comments about Kane, explaining that although he supported fellow Frenchman Kylian Mbappe, he had congratulated the England striker on winning the Ballon d’Or. Henry said he praised Kane for his dedication and work ethic, describing the striker as a deserving winner. “I just said to him [Kane], ‘You are a worthy winner. You deserve it. item.title: Plane reportedly carrying Bolsonaro stops briefly in Ecuador
item.description: The plane that Argentine authorities say is carrying defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro made a brief stop in Ecuador on Wednesday, AFP journalists saw. Argentina’s government said Bolsonaro boarded a private flight operated by the company Baires Fly S.A. bound for the city of Guayaquil, Ecuador, with his wife and two daughters after arriving in Argentina on Tuesday night, despite a court order banning his exit. According to data from the Flightradar24 website, the Baires Fly flight took off just after midnight (0300 GMT) on Wednesday from the Argentine town of Puerto Iguazu in the country’s northeast. That flight landed in Guayaquil shortly before 4:00 a.m. (0900 GMT) before taking off again, AFP journalists and Flightradar24 data confirmed. Bolsonaro’s final destination is unknown, but the US State Department said it would issue visas to the senator and his family. item.title: Nigerian newspapers review: Tinubu seeks $20.5bn, €1.04bn foreign loans to fund projects
item.description: In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with President Bola Tinubu writing to the Senate to seek approval for a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion to finance infrastructure and development projects nationwide. Another headline reports that the Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) agreed on a series of measures to ease the economic difficulties facing workers, including a ₦70,000 transport intervention and payment of 19 months’ arrears owed to health workers. Vanguard also reports that an independent ministerial committee recommended summary dismissal, administrative sanctions and prosecution of some officers of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) over the deaths of 33 detainees in the custody of its Niger State command in Minna, along with N1.4 billion in compensation for victims and survivors. Moving to another newspaper, The Guardian leads with Nigeria’s mounting debt burden coming under heightened scrutiny as President Tinubu seeks legislative approval for fresh external loans of $21.7 billion ($20.52 billion and €1.045 billion), amid rising debt refinancing and little to no savings to liquidate maturing obligations. The Punch reports that Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara asked his supporters to stop referring to him as their leader, declaring that following his reconciliation with his predecessor, Nyesom Wike, he is now a member of the Rainbow Coalition, with the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory as its leader. Lastly, Daily Trust reports that Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani declared his readiness to defend Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, insisting that his support for the president is based on conviction despite public discontent over economic hardship. item.title: Dangote Refinery’s IPO closes with investors from 120 countries
item.description: A Nigerian oil refinery owned by Africa’s richest man Aliko Dangote has closed the continent’s biggest initial public share offering, claiming to have raised funds from investors in 120 countries. The IPO for the Lagos-based Dangote Petroleum Refinery was initially due to close on October 13 but was extended by two weeks to allow more Africans to participate. The company did not disclose how much money was potentially raised by the offering, after saying its target was $1.6 billion. But Aliko Dangote said earlier this month that it had exceeded that goal by “more than three, four times”. “This is a historic achievement for Africa. It shows what is possible when we believe in our continent, work together and invest in our shared future,” he said in a statement late Tuesday. The massive refinery has a capacity of 700,000 barrels per day and aims to double its output to 1.4 million barrels per day, potentially making it the world’s largest refinery, surpassing the Jamnagar refinery in India. Investors from all 54 African countries and five other continents participated in the offering, the company said. “Investor applications spanning 120 countries demonstrate the extraordinary international interest in our business and the confidence that investors are placing in the future of this refinery,” Aliko Dangote said “The opportunity to own a stake in a major African industrial enterprise has reached investors across every African country and all six inhabited continents,” he added. In July, the refinery secured $2.5 billion in investment from private investors. Last month, the company broke ground on a planned $16 billion refinery on Kenya’s Lamu island, with a projected capacity of 700,000 barrels a day. Africa currently imports more than 70 percent of its refined fuel, according to an Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) report in April. item.title: BUA Cement donates ₦12m to families of eight Sokoto crash victims
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto BUA Cement has donated ₦12 million to the families of eight people killed in a road accident along the Kajiji–Tambuwal road in Sokoto State. The company provided ₦1.5 million to each of the bereaved families as financial assistance following the crash, which reportedly involved a commercial minibus conveying 13 passengers and a BUA Cement truck. Eight people, including a child, reportedly died in the accident. The company’s management visited the affected families in Tambuwal to deliver the assistance, accompanied by the District Head of Tambuwal, Alhaji Ahmad Dahiru, and the Chairman of Tambuwal Local Government Area, Hon. Abba Shehu Tambuwal. The donation was commended by the traditional ruler and the council chairman, who described the intervention as a significant demonstration of compassion and support for the bereaved families. The two leaders expressed appreciation to BUA Cement for providing financial assistance despite reports that the company’s truck was not responsible for the accident. They said the gesture demonstrated the importance of corporate social responsibility and urged other organisations to support communities affected by tragedies. The leaders also noted that although the financial assistance could not replace the lives lost, it could help ease some of the immediate financial difficulties confronting the families. They prayed for Allah to reward the company for its generosity, grant eternal rest to the deceased and give their families the strength and patience to bear their losses. The donation comes as the affected households grapple with the loss of their loved ones following the fatal crash. The intervention also highlighted the role of collaboration between businesses, traditional institutions and local government authorities in supporting families affected by emergencies and other tragedies. item.title: New Awujale will emerge before May 29, Abiodun assures Ijebuland
item.description: Governor Dapo Abiodun of Ogun has assured the people of Ijebuland that a new ‘Awujale’ will emerge before May 29. This is contained in a statement in Abeokuta on Wednesday by Abiodun’s Media Adviser, Mr Kayode Akinmade. Abiodun gave the assurance at the Ogun East Senatorial District stakeholders’ meeting in Ijebu-Ode, attended by representatives of various interest groups. The governor explained that his administration was committed to ensuring a peaceful, smooth and acceptable succession process, urging the people to remain calm and patient. “I acknowledge the importance of the Awujale institution to the cultural heritage, identity and unity of Ijebuland, our people should remain calm and patient as the necessary processes are being concluded. “Our administration is giving the matter the attention it deserves, with a view to ensuring that the process is concluded peacefully and the emergence of a new Awujale enjoyed the acceptance and support of the people,” he said. Abiodun said the meeting was organised to strengthen engagement with grassroots stakeholders, address community concerns and showcase his administration’s achievements over the past seven years. On economic development, he identified oil exploration around Eba Island and the proposed Gateway Deep-Sea Port in Ogun Waterside Local Government Area as major growth drivers. He added that the proposed Blue Marine Special Economic Zone would attract investments, create jobs and position Ogun state as a hub for maritime trade, manufacturing and logistics. The governor reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to infrastructure development and investment promotion, appreciating President Bola Tinubu’s support for critical projects and initiatives in the state. He urged continued cooperation to advance peace and development in the state. NAN reports that the Awujale stool became vacant in July 2025 following the passing of Oba Sikiru Adetona at 91 after a 65-year reign. item.title: Onion price jumps 900% to N300,000 in 6 months
item.description: By Cynthia Alo The price of a 120kg bag of onions jumped from N30,000 in April 2026, to about N300,000 in October representing a 900 percent increase in six months. National Onion Producers, Processors and Marketers Association of Nigeria (NOPPMAN) attributed the increase to inadequate storage facilities and fire outbreaks in warehouses in the North which contributed to post-harvest losses of more than 51 percent within the period. A Vanguard AgroBiz market survey shows that the price of a big sack of fresh onions at Mile 12 Lagos international market is N300,000, while the dried one is between N350,000 to N380,000 as of last week. In an interview with Vanguard AgroBiz, the National President of NOPPMAN, Aliyu Isah, said the price surge was not necessarily due to inadequate national production, but rather the loss of a significant proportion of harvested onions before the next production season. “It’s not that we did not produce enough for the country, but we lost more than 51% from April to October,” he said. Isah attributed the losses to poor storage facilities, fires that destroyed onions in local storage centres and the disruption caused by unsuitable seeds introduced into Nigeria during the 2024–2025 growing season. He said the seed, reportedly brought in from Algeria, was unsuitable for Nigeria’s farming system and caused substantial losses to farmers’ investments. According to him, the seed crisis alone resulted in losses estimated at nearly N100bn, while the sector needed government intervention to prevent the disruption from worsening into a supply shortage. He said government intervention was necessary when a crisis affected an agricultural subsector, warning that failure to address the underlying problems could deepen losses in subsequent seasons. Isah said the Ministry of Agriculture had discussed support for the onion subsector with the Bank of Agriculture and the Nigerian Agricultural Development Fund (NADF), regarding seed supply and farm inputs. He said the association had yet to receive the proposed intervention at the time of the interview, although discussions were ongoing. The support, he added, should help farmers restore production and prevent a repeat of the crisis. Looking ahead, Isah expects supplies from Sokoto to begin around November and December, followed by Aliero in Kebbi State from late December to January. The main harvest season is expected around March and April. He expressed optimism that the incoming harvest would ease prices, but said better storage facilities and timely government support were needed to reduce losses and prevent future shortages. item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro on way to Ecuador from Argentina after fleeing Brazil
item.description: Defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro was on his way to Ecuador after fleeing Brazil, Argentina’s government said on Wednesday. Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil’s runoff election to Lula on Sunday, entered Argentina on Tuesday night before boarding a flight to Ecuador, the country’s National Directorate of Migration said on X. The 45-year-old entered Argentina “with valid travel documents and no legal impediment,” it added, despite a court order banning his exit. Bolsonaro, his wife and two daughters boarded “a private flight operated by the company Baires Fly S.A. bound for the city of Guayaquil, Ecuador,” the government agency said. According to data from the Flightradar24 website, the flight took off just after midnight (0300 GMT) on Wednesday from the Argentine town of Puerto Iguazu in the country’s northeast. Baires Fly did not immediately respond to AFP’s request for comment. US media citing anonymous sources had earlier reported that Bolsonaro had arrived in the United States on Tuesday. The US State Department said it would issue visas to Bolsonaro and his family but did not confirm their travel plans. Brazil’s Supreme Court banned Bolsonaro from leaving the country and ordered him to hand over his passports. He is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering, and with his election loss is also set to lose parliamentary immunity. Bolsonaro has not acknowledged his electoral defeat, citing the decision to extend polling hours over transport difficulties that prevented some citizens from voting. item.title: Netanyahu bloc leads after half of Israeli votes counted but no majority
item.description: The camp of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was ahead of his rival’s opposition bloc but still short of a majority on Wednesday after 50 percent of votes were counted in Israel’s pivotal general election. Voters turned out in the highest numbers in decades to give their verdict on Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister who has pushed the country sharply to the right and unleashed a wave of wars in response to Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack. Following the vote, both Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot vowed to form a government despite neither being projected to win a majority. After 51.8 percent of ballots were counted, Netanyahu’s bloc was shown to have 55 of the 120 seats in the parliament. Eisenkot’s opposition bloc had 49 seats and the Arab parties 16. The partial results are likely to change as more votes are counted. Exit polls had shown that Eisenkot, a former military chief and political novice, and his opposition bloc were neck-and-neck with Netanyahu’s hard-right camp, with both winning about 51 seats, well away from the threshold for a majority in parliament. The strongest gains came from Arab Israeli parties whose voters turned out in soaring numbers against Netanyahu, who has relentlessly warned that the minority would dilute the Jewish nationalist direction in which he has taken Israel. The partial results suggest that Eisenkot’s bloc would have enough seats for a majority if there was a coalition agreement with the Arab parties. But Eisenkot said during the campaign he would not govern with Israeli Arab lawmakers, echoing the position of Netanyahu, who has suggested a government relying on Arab votes would lack legitimacy. Arab lawmakers could also give Eisenkot support in parliamentary votes to maintain a minority government without joining a coalition. A lack of clear majority for either camp could mean weeks spent trying to cobble together coalitions, with possible new elections on the horizon if negotiations fail. A stalemate could in the immediate term benefit Netanyahu, who would remain caretaker prime minister until a new government is formed. Full results are expected by Thursday evening or Friday morning. Netanyahu, greeting cheering supporters at a Jerusalem convention centre after 3 am (0100 GMT) on Wednesday morning, called for a “strong government of the right” and said the “Jewish and Zionist majority must unite”. The 77-year-old prime minister, who has governed Israel on and off for nearly two decades, was unusually brief and did not directly claim victory. US President Donald Trump told reporters on Wednesday that his endorsement of Netanyahu had helped the premier “a lot”. – ‘Public voted for change’ – Speaking to supporters in Tel Aviv, 66-year-old Eisenkot issued a veiled warning to Netanyahu, who observers say could use a war to push for a unity government. “Netanyahu, don’t you dare use Israel’s security for your political needs,” Eisenkot said. item.title: Five epic cup shocks after Arsenal’s League Cup humiliation
item.description: Arsenal suffered a stunning League Cup fourth-round defeat at fourth-tier Fleetwood on Tuesday. The Premier League champions lost 5-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in one of the greatest shocks in the history of English football. AFP Sport looks at five other epic cup upsets: Wrexham 2 Arsenal 1 (1992 FA Cup) The previous season 90 places had separated the two clubs in the English Football League, with Arsenal having claimed their second title in three seasons under manager George Graham. Alan Smith put the Gunners in front, but Mickey Thomas’s free-kick levelled matters with 10 minutes remaining and Steve Watkin astonishingly claimed a late winner. Chelsea 2 Bradford 4 (2015 FA Cup) Chelsea won the FA Cup five times between 2006 and 2018, but Jose Mourinho’s Blues were humbled by third tier Bradford at Stamford Bridge. The Premier League leaders went 2-0 up through Gary Cahill and Ramires. But Bradford stormed back and goals from Jon Stead, Filipe Morais, Andy Halliday and Mark Yeates left Chelsea in tatters. Hereford 2 Newcastle 1 (1972 FA Cup) The fourth-round tie that had everything: pitch invasions by Parka-clad fans and Ronnie Radford scoring one of the FA Cup’s greatest FA Cup goals. Malcolm Macdonald put Newcastle ahead eight minutes from time and it seemed as if there would be no fairytale for the non-league outfit. But Radford equalised with a screamer from 25 yards and Ricky George won it for Hereford in extra-time. Liverpool 0 Wimbledon 1 (1988 FA Cup) Wimbledon’s ‘Crazy Gang’ were given no chance to stop Liverpool from claiming a league and cup double in the final at Wembley. Wimbledon had been a third-tier side four years earlier and Liverpool had won the title by a margin of nine points. But Lawrie Sanchez headed home from Dennis Wise’s free-kick before Wimbledon keeper Dave Beasant saved John Aldridge’s penalty to seal the upset. Grimsby 2 Manchester United 2, Grimsby won 12-11 on penalties (2025 League Cup) United trailed 2-0 as Grimsby duo Charles Vernam and Tyrell Warren scored to expose the flaws in their supposedly superior opponents. Bryan Mbeumo and Harry Maguire managed to take the second-round tie into extra-time. But Grimsby won on penalties to leave then-United boss Ruben Amorim shell-shocked. item.title: ‘A very sad day’: Arteta despair as Arsenal stunned by Fleetwood
item.description: Mikel Arteta said Arsenal’s stunning League Cup defeat by fourth-tier Fleetwood was “a very sad day” as the Premier League champions suffered one of the most embarrassing results in their history. Arteta’s side crashed out 5-3 on penalties in an incredible fourth round upset after the tie finished 1-1 in normal time. Arsenal’s Bruno Guimaraes had his penalty saved by Jay Lynch in the shoot-out and Conor Haughey scored Fleetwood’s winner. Aaron Loupalo-Bi’s first-half goal had put Fleetwood ahead before Viktor Gyokeres equalised after the interval. Arsenal’s 16-year-old rising star Max Dowman was sent off for violent conduct in the closing stages. Arteta paid the price for prioritising Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool as his decision to make nine changes backfired spectacularly. The Gunners boss conceded Arsenal could have no complaints, admitting it was a painful moment in his reign. “First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood for going through the next round. The manner that they have done it, and for us a very sad day,” Arteta said. “There is nothing to criticise the players for their attitude, their application. “The determination, you could see that was there from the start, even with 10 men. But we conceded a really poor goal to start with that gave them some momentum. “Obviously we have so much of the ball, so many chances, so many shots, and if you want the margins to be bigger than going to the penalties, you need to capitalise on that. And we didn’t. “It’s football, that’s the beauty of this competition. It’s a very sad day.” Arsenal had moved level on points with Premier League leaders Manchester City after a 2-0 victory over Everton on Saturday. But instead of extending their run of 11 wins from their 13 previous games, Arteta’s team returned to north London red-faced after a loss that ranks among the darkest days in the club’s glittering history. “Zero problem attitude-wise. Otherwise, I would be here absolutely fuming. I’m sad, I think we are all sad. We have a massive responsibility to carry this badge in the best possible way,” Arteta said. “You don’t capitalise, then you cannot go through to the next round. Unfortunately, we are out.” – ‘I just can’t believe it’ – Although it looked a harsh decision to send off Dowman for aiming a kick towards Harrison Neal, Arteta was unimpressed with the 16-year-old, giving him a stern word as the midfielder trudged off. “Something that we discussed already before the match,” Arteta said when asked what he told Dowman. “It’s difficult to see on the cameras like that, so I prefer to watch it back properly and then I can assess the situation.” Fleetwood made a mockery of the 84 places between the clubs in the English football system with a defiant display that stopped Arsenal establishing any momentum. item.title: Nigerian extradited from Benin to US over alleged $100m tax fraud
item.description: A 43-year-old Nigerian, Akinade Adedeji Raheem, has been extradited from Benin to the United States to face federal charges over an alleged scheme involving more than $100 million in fraudulent tax refund claims using stolen identities. Raheem was arraigned in a US federal court following his extradition and ordered detained in the custody of the US Marshals Service pending further proceedings, according to the US Department of Justice. Prosecutors alleged that Raheem and his co-conspirators filed more than 300 fraudulent tax returns between 2018 and 2023, seeking over $100 million in refunds from the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). US Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg said the alleged operation involved hundreds of stolen identities and significant financial losses. “Raheem and his co-conspirators allegedly obtained hundreds of stolen identities, filed fraudulent tax returns using that information, and laundered the proceeds through prepaid debit cards and purchases of used cars that were shipped to Nigeria and other locations,” Hertzberg said. “The scope of the alleged fraud is staggering. Thanks to the dedication of the prosecution team and our law enforcement partners around the world, Raheem has been extradited to the United States,” he added. The indictment also named Abayomi Quadri Eletu, a resident of the United Kingdom and Nigeria, as an alleged co-conspirator. Eletu was indicted separately and arrested in the UK, where extradition proceedings are pending. According to court documents, the suspects allegedly obtained the personal information of American taxpayers and tax professionals, including names, addresses and Social Security numbers, to facilitate fraudulent claims. Investigators said the alleged scheme involved creating online IRS accounts to access private taxpayer information, filing false returns and directing refunds to prepaid debit cards linked to addresses controlled by the suspects. Prosecutors further alleged that Raheem, Eletu and others laundered some of the proceeds by purchasing money orders in amounts intended to avoid reporting requirements. The money was allegedly used to acquire used cars through auction platforms, some of which were shipped to Nigeria, as well as designer clothing and other items. Special Agent in Charge Christopher J. Altemus Jr. of the IRS Criminal Investigation Texas Field Office said the alleged scheme affected hundreds of taxpayers. “Raheem is an alleged co-conspirator in a nationwide identity theft scheme that victimised hundreds of taxpayers. The fraud also stole from the US Treasury, impacting programmes serving us all,” Altemus said. He added that authorities were working internationally to bring suspects in financial crimes to justice. “We are pursuing financial criminals to take back the stolen money and their freedom,” he said. item.title: French Senate passes bill to make protesters pay for unrest damage
item.description: The French parliament’s upper house passed a bill Wednesday that would make protesters financially liable for damage caused during street demonstrations, despite warnings from critics that it could curb the right to protest. The bill was drafted in response to riots that followed Paris Saint-Germain’s victory over Arsenal in the UEFA Champions League final in May. But it has taken on added significance after weeks of protests over inequality and soaring prices culminated in some of the worst violence France has seen in years on October 17, when thousands of businesses across the country were damaged and looted. The Senate passed an expanded version of the bill by 229 votes to 105, backed by a right-wing and centrist alliance which holds a majority. The legislation has been sent to the National Assembly, which is split between France’s political factions, for debate and voting. Far-right leader Marine Le Pen, whom opinion polls place as the frontrunner to succeed Emmanuel Macron in next spring’s presidential election, supports the legislation. Speaking in parliament, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez stressed the “urgency” of responding to the damage and scenes of chaos seen on October 17. “We can no longer allow the vast majority of our fellow citizens to pay for a minority of vandals,” he said. – ‘Legal travesty’ – Under the legislation, protesters could be ordered to pay up to 10,000 euros for damage caused during street demonstrations. But critics argue that people who took no part in vandalism could nonetheless be held liable if they were deemed to have been associated with those responsible. The bill introduces joint financial liability for anyone found to have “knowingly participated” in a group formed with the intent of carrying out acts of vandalism. It would also apply to individuals who “voluntarily” continued to take part in a gathering likely to disrupt public order after two police dispersal warnings. Welfare benefits and housing assistance could also be seized to help cover the cost of damages under the scheme, a provision that has drawn sharp criticism from left-wing parties and advocacy groups. In the second reading, senators toughened the measure to include other social benefits such as the family supplement, back-to-school allowance and the employment bonus. Left-wing lawmakers accused the government of an “authoritarian drift” at the expense of the freedom to demonstrate. Communist senator Fabien Gay denounced what he called a “legal travesty that deliberately conflates protesters and rioters”. Green senator Melanie Vogel accused the government of responding to social demands with “collective punishment.” Supporters of the bill sought to reassure critics. “We must not give the impression that this bill would criminalise a passer-by or a peaceful protester,” said Olivier Bitz of the centre-right Horizons party. – ‘Disastrous consequences’ – The government has proposed introducing protest bans targeting the most violent individuals
